title: Tyvaren's Answer
dialogue: Tyvaren has moved beyond diplomatic protests. Dusek requested the briefing.
monologue: When Dusek requests a briefing rather than waiting for the scheduled one, the situation has moved faster than the schedule.

narrative.text: Tyvaren has suspended the three bilateral trade agreements they declined to renew last month. The suspension is formal — it triggers economic provisions in the original agreements that Veltria will need to address. The annual impact is approximately twelve million kroner in trade disruption.
They have also conducted two additional naval exercises in the Thalassic zone this week. Both within legal parameters. Both visible from the Sevagrad construction site.

This is calibrated escalation. They are applying economic and military pressure simultaneously to test whether the Sovarka partnership holds under sustained cost. The correct response is to demonstrate that it does.

tyvaren_response_brief.monologue: Twelve million kroner in trade disruption and naval exercises visible from our port construction site. They are making sure we know the cost of the Sovarka decision every week. Vyktor says demonstrate that the partnership holds. That is the correct policy answer. It is also the expensive one.

choices.text: "Hold the line. The partnership stands. Find alternative trade arrangements to replace the suspended agreements."
"Open a back channel to Tyvaren. The partnership with Sovarka is not negotiable. The trade agreements may be."
